seoTitle: How to Keep a Trading Journal Directly in TradingView
metaDescription: Learn how to journal your trades in TradingView using notes, Paper Trading history, and export options to track buy and sell decisions over time.
intro: Keeping a consistent trading journal is one of the most effective ways to improve as a trader, and TradingView offers several built-in ways to log your buy and sell activity. This guide covers using Paper Trading history, adding notes directly on the chart, and exporting trade data for deeper review. It's aimed at traders who want more discipline and better performance tracking over time.

steps.heading: Understand why a trading journal matters
steps.body: Logging your trades consistently helps you spot patterns in your decision-making and identify what's actually working in your strategy.

steps.heading: Use Paper Trading history
steps.body: Review your Paper Trading history as a built-in log of past buy and sell decisions, complete with timestamps and prices.

steps.heading: Add notes directly on the chart
steps.body: Use TradingView's text and note tools to label specific entries, exits, or reasoning right on the chart where the trade happened.

steps.heading: Export trade data for analysis
steps.body: Export your trade history where possible so you can review performance metrics outside of TradingView, such as in a spreadsheet.

steps.heading: Follow best practices for a consistent journal
steps.body: Log every trade, not just the winners, and review your journal regularly to reinforce good habits and correct recurring mistakes.

faq.question: Does TradingView have a dedicated trading journal feature?
faq.answer: TradingView doesn't have one single formal journal feature, but Paper Trading history and chart notes together can serve as an effective journaling system.

faq.question: Can I add notes to specific price points on my chart?
faq.answer: Yes, TradingView's text and drawing tools let you label specific entries, exits, or reasoning directly on the chart.

faq.question: How do I export my trade history from TradingView?
faq.answer: Depending on your account and trading setup, you may be able to export Paper Trading history for use in an external spreadsheet or journal.

faq.question: Why should I journal losing trades too, not just wins?
faq.answer: Reviewing losing trades helps you spot recurring mistakes and refine your strategy, which is just as valuable as studying your wins.
